# 2026 US Senate Elections (Nov 3, 2026): Fact Check of Claimed Winners and "Firsts"

All findings below come from pages retrieved on Nov 8, 2026 in this session. Nothing is confirmed from training memory. Where a fact rests only on my background knowledge, it is labelled as such and left UNVERIFIED.

Source-quality note: most results come from AP stories syndicated by local TV stations (Gray, Sinclair, Scripps, Cox), NPR member stations, CBS, Fox News, Al Jazeera, and Ballotpedia. Vote shares quoted from local results pages are partial counts taken on election night, not certified totals. Axios (Texas) could not be fetched.

## Overall Senate and House outcome as of Nov 8, 2026

### Takeaway
Democrats won control of the Senate. The AP called the chamber on election night. The AP tally was 54 D, 44 R, with 2 seats uncalled (as of Nov 4). Ballotpedia (as of Nov 6) shows 7 seats flipped, all from Republican to Democratic, with 2 races uncalled, both previously Republican. The AP House tally had Democrats at 225 seats with 73 races uncalled (as of Nov 4). 225 is above the 218 needed for a majority.

### Cited Findings
- The AP called the Senate for Democrats late on Nov 3. Democrats had at least 54 seats after needing a net gain of four. — [Al Jazeera](https://aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/4/democratic-party-flips-us-senate-in-2026-midterm-elections)
- Flips listed by Al Jazeera: SC (Andrews over Darline Graham), NC (Roy Cooper over Michael Whatley), TX (Talarico over Paxton), OH (Sherrod Brown over Jon Husted), KS (Adam Hamilton over Roger Marshall), ME (Troy Jackson over Susan Collins), IA (Josh Turek over Ashley Hinson). Michigan was a hold, not a flip. — [Al Jazeera](https://aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/4/democratic-party-flips-us-senate-in-2026-midterm-elections)
- Ballotpedia, as of 4:00 PM ET Nov 6: of 35 races, D won 20 and R won 13. Seven seats changed party, all R to D. Two races were uncalled, both previously held by Republicans, but the page does not name them. Ballotpedia cites a Decision Desk HQ projection of Democratic control, and lists post-election chamber totals as "Pending." — [Ballotpedia](https://ballotpedia.org/United_States_Senate_elections,_2026)
- The AP tally reported Nov 4: Senate D 54, R 44, 2 to call. House D 225, R 137, 73 to call. Governors D 26, R 20, 4 to call. — [Newcastle Herald (AAP), "Democrats take full control of Congress"](https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/9386125/democrats-take-full-control-of-congress-in-midterms/)
- Al Jazeera named Alaska as a key toss-up but did not report its result. — [Al Jazeera](https://aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/4/democratic-party-flips-us-senate-in-2026-midterm-elections)

### Inferences
- Net Senate change is at least D+7. Pre-election the split was 53 R and 47 D (including independents). That baseline is from memory, but it matches 47 + 7 = 54. If either uncalled R-held seat flips, the gain would be D+8 or D+9.
- The House: 225 D seats in the AP tally exceeds 218, which implies a Democratic majority. I did not retrieve a page that names the outlet or time of a formal House call.

### Gaps
- The names of the 2 uncalled Senate races were not found. Alaska is a possibility but is unconfirmed.
- No formal House-control call (outlet and time) was retrieved, and no updated Nov 7–8 tallies were found.

## Claim 1: Abdul El-Sayed (D, Michigan)

### Takeaway
Confirmed. He won (AP projection) over Mike Rogers, about 53–45 on partial returns. He narrowly won the August 5 primary over Haley Stevens. He is widely reported as the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. One detail is missing a source: manufacturing jobs as a campaign theme.

### Cited Findings
- AP projected El-Sayed the winner. With 89.4% of precincts reporting: El-Sayed 2,520,388 (53%), Rogers 2,180,541 (45%), Libertarian 1%. The page was published Nov 4 at 2:28 AM. — [ClickOnDetroit/WDIV](https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/local/2026/11/04/abdul-el-sayed-wins-michigan-us-senate-race-ap-projects/)
- He was set to win more than 52% with over 95% tallied. He is "the first Muslim elected to the US Senate," described as a physician and former public health official who worked as an epidemiologist. He led Detroit's Health Department as executive director and supports Medicare for All. He criticizes corporate influence in Washington. — [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/11/4/call-me-senator-how-abdul-el-sayed-beat-trumps-hate-to-create-history)
- Other outlets report the same "first Muslim elected to US Senate" claim. — [Anadolu](https://aa.com.tr/en/world/abdul-el-sayed-becomes-1st-muslim-elected-to-us-senate-in-michigan-win/4110982); [TheGrio](https://thegrio.com/2026/11/04/abdul-el-sayed-makes-history-as-first-muslim-elected-to-u-s-senate-in-michigan/)
- Primary (Aug 5, 2026), AP projected El-Sayed. At 86% reporting: El-Sayed 743,441 (49%), Stevens 727,747 (47%), McMorrow 61,407 (4%). The page also says he directed Wayne County's Department of Health, Human, and Veterans Services from 2023 to 2025. — [ClickOnDetroit](https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/local/2026/08/05/abdul-el-sayed-wins-2026-michigan-us-senate-democratic-primary-election-ap-projects/)
- More than $50M was spent in the primary, at least $30M of it by AIPAC backing Stevens. — [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/11/4/call-me-senator-how-abdul-el-sayed-beat-trumps-hate-to-create-history)
- The "progressive wing" framing appears in reporting of a "progressive" duel and in primary coverage. — [ABC7](https://abc7news.com/post/2026-elections-progressive-democrat-abdul-el-sayed-republican-mike-rogers-duel-key-michigan-us-senate-seat/20012775/)

### Verdicts
| Claim | Verdict | Note / Source |
|---|---|---|
| Won | CONFIRMED | AP projection, about 53–45 partial (WDIV) |
| Defeated Mike Rogers | CONFIRMED | WDIV |
| First Muslim US senator | CONFIRMED (as "first Muslim elected") | Al Jazeera, Anadolu, TheGrio. Sources say "elected." A prior appointed Muslim senator is not explicitly ruled out, but none is mentioned. |
| Physician / epidemiologist | CONFIRMED | Al Jazeera |
| Former Detroit health director | CONFIRMED | Al Jazeera. He also led Wayne County's health department 2023–25 (WDIV). |
| Progressive wing | CONFIRMED | ABC7, WDIV |
| Medicare for All | CONFIRMED | Al Jazeera |
| Corporate PAC influence | PARTLY: CORRECTED | Al Jazeera says "corporate influence." PAC-specific framing is not sourced. |
| Public health | CONFIRMED | Al Jazeera |
| Manufacturing jobs | UNVERIFIED | Not found in retrieved pages |
| Won Aug primary vs Stevens, McMorrow | CONFIRMED | 49–47–4 at 86% (WDIV). The primary was Aug 5. |
| Has any Muslim served in Senate before | No prior Muslim senator mentioned. "First Muslim elected" is confirmed. | See above |

### Gaps
- Certified final vote totals.
- The years he served as Detroit health director were not given in retrieved sources.

## Claim 2: Peggy Flanagan (D, Minnesota)

### Takeaway
She won (AP called it at 12:07 a.m. EST) over Republican Michele Tafoya. She beat Angie Craig 59.0–39.4 in the Aug 11 primary. She is the current Lieutenant Governor, not former. The "first Native American woman senator" claim was not stated in any retrieved source.

### Cited Findings
- AP declared Flanagan the winner at 12:07 a.m. EST, defeating Republican Michele Tafoya. She is a member of the Ojibwe tribe, the "current lieutenant governor," and succeeds retiring Sen. Tina Smith. No vote shares were given. — [KTTC (AP)](https://www.kttc.com/2026/11/04/democrat-peggy-flanagan-wins-election-us-senate-minnesota/?outputType=amp)
- Primary Aug 11, 2026: Flanagan 59.0% (411,853) vs Craig 39.4% (274,920), called by AP and NBC. Sanders and Warren endorsed her. After an ICE agent killed Renée Good, she called for a "complete and total overhaul" of ICE and later backed dismantling and replacing it. She has been Lt. Gov. since 2019. — [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_election_in_Minnesota)
- Ballotpedia: Flanagan defeated Craig and four others in the Aug 11 primary. — [Ballotpedia News](https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/08/13/peggy-flanagan-d-defeated-angie-craig-d-and-four-other-candidates-in-the-democratic-primary-for-u-s-senate-in-minnesota-on-august-11-2026/)

### Verdicts
| Claim | Verdict | Note / Source |
|---|---|---|
| Won | CONFIRMED | AP, 12:07 a.m. EST (KTTC) |
| Republican opponent | Michele Tafoya | KTTC |
| First Native American female US senator | UNVERIFIED | Not stated in retrieved sources. Ojibwe membership is confirmed (KTTC). |
| Minnesota's first Native American senator | UNVERIFIED | Not stated in retrieved sources |
| Former Lt. Gov. | CORRECTED | She is the current Lt. Gov. (KTTC, Wikipedia) |
| Endorsed by Sanders and Warren | CONFIRMED | Wikipedia |
| Opposition to mass deportations/ICE | CONFIRMED | Wikipedia |
| Paid family leave | UNVERIFIED | Not found |
| Tribal sovereignty | UNVERIFIED | Not found |
| Beat Angie Craig in primary | CONFIRMED | 59.0–39.4, Aug 11 (Wikipedia, Ballotpedia) |
| Any Native American woman in Senate before | UNVERIFIED | No retrieved source addresses it |

### Gaps
- General-election vote shares.
- No retrieved source states the "first Native American woman" historic claim. It needs a targeted check (for example a Senate Historical Office list) before publication.

## Claim 3: Chris Pappas (D, New Hampshire)

### Takeaway
Confirmed. He won the open seat (Shaheen retired) over former GOP Sen. John E. Sununu. Multiple outlets report he will be the first openly gay male US senator. CBS projected the race, and Sununu conceded about 10 minutes after polls closed.

### Cited Findings
- Pappas defeated former US Sen. John E. Sununu. The win makes him the "first openly gay male U.S. senator." He has represented NH-01 since 2019. Sununu conceded about 10 minutes after the last polls closed. The seat was being vacated by three-term Sen. Jeanne Shaheen. — [WPTV (Scripps)](https://www.wptv.com/politics/america-votes/chris-pappas-wins-new-hampshire-senate-race-becoming-first-openly-gay-male-senator)
- CBS News projected Pappas the winner. The seat opened after Shaheen's retirement. — [CBS News](https://cbsnews.com/news/new-hampshire-2026-senate-pappas-sununu)
- Headline: "Democrat Chris Pappas to become first openly gay male US senator." — [WJLA](https://wjla.com/news/nation-world/democrat-chris-pappas-wins-new-hampshires-open-us-senate-seat-john-e-sununu-election-day-midterms-midterm-elections-politics-vote-voting-voters-taxpayers-polls-ballots-congress-president-donald-trump)

### Verdicts
| Claim | Verdict | Note / Source |
|---|---|---|
| Won | CONFIRMED | CBS projection |
| First openly gay male US senator | CONFIRMED (as reported) | WPTV, WJLA. No source discussed Baldwin or Sinema. |
| Four-term congressman (NH-01) | CONFIRMED by inference | Sources say "since 2019." That implies elections in 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2024, which is four terms. |
| Opponent | John E. Sununu (not Scott Brown) | WPTV, CBS |

### Gaps
- Vote shares and margin were not retrieved.

## Claim 4: Annie Andrews (D, South Carolina)

### Takeaway
This claim is largely TRUE, though it sounds implausible. Lindsey Graham died in office in July 2026. His sister Darline Graham was appointed to the seat by Gov. Henry McMaster, not by Trump. Trump backed her in the special GOP primary and campaign. Andrews beat her 50.6–47.2 (AP call 10:39 p.m. EST). She is the first woman ever elected to the US Senate from SC, and the first Democrat elected to the Senate from SC since Fritz Hollings in 1998.

### Cited Findings
- AP called the race for Andrews at 10:39 p.m. EST Nov 3: Andrews 50.6%, Graham 47.2% at that time. Darline Graham is the "younger sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham." He died July 11 from "a believed tear in his aorta," and she was appointed in July 2026. — [WBTV (AP)](https://www.wbtv.com/2026/11/04/democrat-annie-andrews-wins-us-senate-seat-south-carolina-ap-projects/)
- Gov. McMaster appointed Darline Graham to finish the term. McMaster said he spoke with Trump, who thought the pick was a great idea. Lindsey Graham died at 71 on a Saturday. The term runs to Jan 3, 2027. A special GOP primary was set for Aug 11. — [HPPR (NPR)](https://www.hppr.org/2026-07-14/south-carolinas-governor-appoints-lindsey-grahams-sister-to-serve-out-his-term)
- WIS reported that McMaster would name a replacement after Graham's death (Jul 13). — [WIS](https://www.wistv.com/2026/07/13/mcmaster-announce-replacement-us-senate-after-death-lindsey-graham/)
- Fox News Decision Desk projected Andrews at 10:16 p.m. EST. Trump backed Darline Graham in the special primary, which she won in a late-August runoff over Rep. Ralph Norman, and rallied with her twice. Lindsey Graham had won renomination in June before he died. Andrews is a pediatrician, and she is the first Democrat in nearly three decades to win a Senate election in SC. — [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/massive-upset-andrews-downs-trump-backed-graham-ruby-red-south-carolina.amp)
- Andrews is "the first woman ever elected" to the US Senate from SC. The last Democrat elected was Fritz Hollings in 1998. Schumer described her as a pediatrician with 20 years in health care. — [WLOS/WCIV (Sinclair)](https://wlos.com/news/local/south-carolina-elects-democrat-annie-andrews-to-us-senate-first-since-1998-wciv-abc-news-4-election-day-polls-donald-trump-senate-house-election-results-washington-dc)
- Ballotpedia lists Darline Graham as the pre-election incumbent. — [Ballotpedia](https://ballotpedia.org/United_States_Senate_elections,_2026)

### Verdicts
| Claim | Verdict | Note / Source |
|---|---|---|
| Won | CONFIRMED | AP, 10:39 p.m. EST, 50.6–47.2 at call (WBTV) |
| SC's first elected female US senator | CONFIRMED | WLOS/WCIV |
| Flipped a seat held by GOP about 30 years | CORRECTED | The roughly 28–30 years refers to the last time a Democrat won any SC Senate race (Hollings, 1998). Graham held this seat from 2003 (WBTV). The seat's earlier R history (Thurmond) is from memory and unverified here. Either way it is not "about 30 years." |
| Pediatrician | CONFIRMED | Fox, WLOS |
| Lindsey Graham died | CONFIRMED | Jul 11, 2026, believed aortic tear (WBTV, HPPR) |
| Opponent Darline Graham, interim senator | CONFIRMED | Spelled "Darline" (Fox metadata also shows "Darlene") |
| "Trump-appointed" | FALSE / CORRECTED | Appointed by Gov. Henry McMaster. Trump approved of the pick and endorsed her (HPPR, Fox). |

### Gaps
- Final certified vote totals.

## Claim 5: James Talarico (D, Texas)

### Takeaway
He won, but he defeated Ken Paxton, not John Cornyn. Paxton beat Cornyn in the May 26 GOP runoff. Talarico won the March Democratic primary (Crockett was his opponent). AP called the general at 10:03 p.m. CT. He led 55–43 with about 99% reporting. Sources frame this as the first Democratic Senate win in Texas since 1988.

### Cited Findings
- Talarico won the Democratic primary, while Cornyn and Paxton went to a GOP runoff. Headline framing: "Democrats Crockett, Talarico face off." — [WTOP (AP, Mar 2026)](https://wtop.com/national/2026/03/texas-gop-sen-cornyn-tries-to-hold-his-seat-while-democrats-crockett-talarico-face-off-for-senate/); [States Newsroom](https://sourcenm.com/2026/03/04/repub/talarico-wins-democratic-primary-for-us-senate-in-texas-cornyn-and-paxton-go-to-gop-runoff/)
- Paxton, backed by Trump, defeated incumbent Cornyn in the GOP runoff (dated May 26, 2026 per photo caption), according to CBS projections. — [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/texas-senate-gop-runoff-results-paxton-cornyn-trump-talarico/)
- Results page at 99% of precincts: Talarico 5,446,309 (55%), Paxton 4,250,166 (43%), Ted Brown (L) 190,293 (2%). — [KPRC Click2Houston](https://www.click2houston.com/decision-2026/2026/11/02/texas-us-senate-election-results-ken-paxton-vs-james-talarico/)
- AP called the race at 10:03 p.m. CT Nov 3. It is the first Democratic Senate victory in Texas since 1988. The page contains inconsistent figures: one summary says "nearly 60%," and streak lengths of 32, 36, and 38 years appear. — [Straight Arrow News](https://san.com/cc/james-talarico-defeats-ken-paxton-flips-texas-senate-seat-for-first-time-since-1988/)
- Axios headline: "Talarico flips Texas Senate seat, ending 38-year Democratic drought." The page was not fetchable. — [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/04/texas-senate-results-talarico-paxton)

### Verdicts
| Claim | Verdict | Note / Source |
|---|---|---|
| Won | CONFIRMED | AP 10:03 p.m. CT (SAN). About 55–43 (KPRC). |
| Defeated John Cornyn | FALSE / CORRECTED | He defeated Ken Paxton. Cornyn lost the May 26 GOP runoff (CBS). |
| First Democratic senator from TX since 1993 | PARTLY CORRECTED | Sources frame it as the first Democratic Senate election win since 1988. "Since 1993" would be accurate only for a Democrat serving: Bentsen left in Jan 1993, but that is from memory and not verified in this session. Prefer "first Democrat elected since 1988." |
| Democratic primary | Talarico won (March 3, 2026) over Jasmine Crockett | WTOP, States Newsroom. Colin Allred's status is unverified. |
| Republican primary/runoff | Paxton beat Cornyn in the runoff. Wesley Hunt's role is unverified. | CBS |

### Gaps
- Primary vote shares, and whether Allred and Hunt were on the ballot.

## Claim 6: Jon Ossoff (D, Georgia)

### Takeaway
Re-elected. AP called the race at 7:55 p.m. EST, and he defeated Republican Rep. Mike Collins "easily." No retrieved source makes or supports the claim that he is the "first Jewish senator from Georgia to win re-election."

### Cited Findings
- AP called the race for Ossoff at 7:55 p.m. EST Nov 3 over Mike Collins, a two-term congressman endorsed by Trump. — [OPB (AP)](https://www.opb.org/article/2026/11/03/democrat-jon-ossoff-wins-reelection-to-u-s-senate-from-georgia/)
- NPR reported Ossoff "easily" defeated Collins. AP was the caller, and no shares were given. — [WFAE (NPR)](https://www.wfae.org/united-states-world/2026-11-03/jon-ossoff-wins-reelection-in-georgia-easily-defeating-republican-mike-collins)

### Verdicts
| Claim | Verdict | Note / Source |
|---|---|---|
| Re-elected | CONFIRMED | AP 7:55 p.m. EST (OPB) |
| Opponent | Mike Collins (not Buddy Carter or Derek Dooley) | OPB |
| First Jewish senator from Georgia to win re-election | UNVERIFIED | Not found in any retrieved source. Do not publish without a source. |

### Gaps
- Vote shares and margin.
- No source was found for the "first Jewish ... re-election" claim.
